tools.note: SigMA's DESCRIPTION hard-Imports BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19. That package's bioconda post-link.sh only fetches from bioconductor.org / bioarchive.galaxyproject.org / depot.galaxyproject.org, all three confirmed blocked by this environment's network egress policy (403 at the proxy for each, see ENVIRONMENT.lock §2). Unlike bioconductor-genomeinfodbdata (successfully rebuilt locally, see docker/local_channel/), this package could not be rebuilt from its canonical Bioconductor GitHub mirror this session: add_repo refused a third external-owner repo attachment ('cross-tier adds are not supported in v1'), and the repo's actual sequence data is git-lfs-tracked in any case, which this session's anonymous git-clone lane does not serve. A few plausible alternate hosts (bioconductorhubs.blob.core.windows.net, annotationhub.bioconductor.org, experimenthub.bioconductor.org) were also checked and are also blocked. This is reported as FAIL, not substituted with another tool: the task requires SigProfilerAssignment AND SigMA specifically, with no 'or equivalent' allowance for SigMA.

resolution_attempts_p08.result: FAILED: BiocManager itself is not installable -- "cannot open URL 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES'" (cran.r-project.org network-blocked, consistent with the mirror-blocking already documented in ENVIRONMENT.lock).

resolution_attempts_p08.attempt: conda install -n bioenv -c bioconda -c conda-forge bioconductor-bsgenome.hsapiens.ucsc.hg19 (dry-run)
resolution_attempts_p08.result: FAILED, but with a NEW and DIFFERENT reason than the network-mirror block: the conda solver resolved channel metadata successfully this time and reported a genuine version conflict -- bioconductor-bsgenome.hsapiens.ucsc.hg19 1.4.0 requires r-base pinned to old versions (3.2.2/3.3.1/3.4.1), incompatible with this bioenv environment's modern R pin. Even if the network block were lifted, this specific conda environment could not install this package cleanly without a separate/older R environment (LibMambaUnsatisfiableError, full solver output not reproduced here).

resolution_attempts_p08.attempt: conda install of the hg38 BSgenome variant (bioconductor-bsgenome.hsapiens.ucsc.hg38), to test whether SigMA's DESCRIPTION could be satisfied by a different build
resolution_attempts_p08.result: INCONCLUSIVE: did not complete within an operationally reasonable time budget in this session (solver did not return within ~90-120s, vs. the hg19 attempt which did). Not pursued further. Separately, SigMA's DESCRIPTION Imports field hard-codes BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19 specifically (not a generic BSgenome dependency) -- even though SigMA's own R/make_matrix.R code supports an hg38 ref_genome argument, R's package installer checks the DESCRIPTION literally and would still refuse to install without the hg19 package present, regardless of which genome build is used at runtime. An hg38 substitution would require patching SigMA's DESCRIPTION, not just installing a different BSgenome package.

resolution_attempts_p08.attempt: Source-level bypass: source() SigMA's R/*.R files directly (skipping normal package install), omitting only the 3 files that reference BSgenome (R/get_trinuc_norm.R, R/make_matrix.R, R/mmej_nhej_indels_from_vcfs.R -- all VCF/genome-coordinate-to-matrix conversion utilities), then load R/sysdata.rda (internal trained models) and call the package's own analysis-entrypoint functions.
resolution_attempts_p08.result: PARTIAL SUCCESS: 20/20 non-BSgenome R files sourced without error; sysdata.rda loaded; list_data_options() executed successfully and printed all supported sequencing-platform settings including 'seqcap' (Whole Exome Sequencing 37 Mb) -- the regime this study is in. All of SigMA's OTHER declared dependencies (BSgenome, devtools, DT, GenomicRanges, ggplot2, gbm, gridExtra, IRanges, nnls, reshape2, Rmisc, VariantAnnotation) are already installed in this environment. list_tumor_types() failed on a path-resolution error ('cannot open the connection'), because the package is not actually installed (system.file()-style internal data lookups do not resolve from a bare source checkout). CONCLUSION: SigMA's core signature-analysis machinery (NNLS decomposition, likelihood/gbm scoring against a pre-built mutation-count matrix -- run()'s genome_file/input_df argument) is NOT itself blocked by BSgenome; only the VCF-to-matrix conversion utility is. This was NOT taken further to a full run against this study's simulated catalogs: doing so would require (a) mapping this repo's 'A[C>A]A'-style 96-context column labels to SigMA's own lowercase 4-character context convention, a nontrivial correspondence not yet verified, and (b) resolving the tumor-type/data-setting model lookup that failed above. Treated as an unresolved, incomplete avenue -- SigMA is NOT run against this study's data, and this partial bypass does not change the gate status below.

resolution_attempts_p06r2.attempt: Completed the P08 catalogue-only avenue: derived the exact COSMIC-to-SigMA 96-context label mapping from SigMA's own R/make_matrix.R (.make_type(): type = tolower(paste0(ref_base, alt_base, prime5, prime3)), then sort() -- confirmed by direct comparison against SigMA's own bundled examples/example_mmrd_SBS_matrix.csv header, e.g. COSMIC 'A[C>A]A' -> SigMA 'caaa'), built a genome_file CSV from 10 real samples in the P06R2-fixed SIMULATED_mutation_catalogs.tsv (5 CORE_HR Pathogenic with true sbs3_relative_exposure_true 0.76-0.84, 5 CORE_HR Benign with true exposure exactly 0.0), sourced the same 20 non-BSgenome R files + sysdata.rda as the P08 bypass, and called the real run(genome_file=..., data='seqcap', tumor_type='breast', catalog_name='cosmic_v2_inhouse', do_mva=FALSE) end to end.
resolution_attempts_p06r2.result: SUCCESS -- SigMA's real likelihood-based signature-matching algorithm ran to completion against this study's own (post-P06R2-fix, real-COSMIC-shaped) simulated data. Result: 10/10 samples classified correctly by sig_max_wl -- all 5 true-high-SBS3-exposure Pathogenic samples matched to 'Signature_3' (max_wl 0.9999955-1.0), all 5 true-zero-SBS3-exposure Benign samples matched to 'Signature_5' (max_wl 0.6421-1.0). The continuous rat_sig3 score also separated cleanly (Pathogenic: 0.44-0.86; Benign: 0.00-0.28). Full result: SIMULATED_signature_work/SIMULATED_sigma_catalogue_only_attempt_result.csv; input: SIMULATED_signature_work/SIMULATED_sigma_catalogue_only_genome_file.csv. CAVEATS, stated plainly: (1) n=10, a small demonstration set deliberately chosen to span true exposure extremes, not a calibrated validation at the scale of Task K/P08's SigProfilerAssignment runs (n=382 stratified subsample); (2) this is the source-level bypass, not the formally gated `R CMD INSTALL` path this GATE1 entry's own status/exit_code/test_command test -- BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19 remains genuinely absent and the formal install still fails identically to before (see status/exit_code/output_excerpt above, unchanged); this success does NOT flip this entry's status to PASS. IMPLICATION (not acted on): SigMA's likelihood-based approach appears to succeed at exactly the exome-scale, low-mutation-count regime where P08 found real SigProfilerAssignment's NNLS decomposition genuinely unstable (DIAGNOSIS_P08.md §5) -- consistent with SigMA's own DESCRIPTION claim of being 'optimized to detect...Signature 3...from...exomes' for 'panels with low SNV counts.' This bears on PROTOCOL.md §5.4's tool choice, but PROTOCOL.md is not modified by this task; see TRUTH_DELTA.md's SigMA appendix.
